text:
You want to learn by building a clone of a specific web app with card and PayPal checkout/subscriptions, and you need someone who can guide you through the full stack while keeping the project practical and manageable.

I’m Tobias Reyne, and I’ve spent 7 years working with JavaScript and TypeScript across React, Next.js, Node.js, PostgreSQL, REST APIs, Tailwind CSS, Stripe, HTML, and CSS. That background is a good fit for this kind of learning-focused build, because I can help you understand not just how to make the pages look right, but how the app actually works behind the scenes.

For a booking platform for fitness studios, I built a white-label class booking app with subdomains, timetables, memberships, and Stripe-based subscription billing. That project onboarded 64 studios in 6 months and reached a 71% checkout conversion rate. It’s relevant here because it involved structuring a multi-tenant product flow and payment logic in a way that was clean enough to maintain and explain.

I also rebuilt a home goods storefront as a headless Next.js site with Tailwind CSS and Stripe. The result was a faster storefront with the largest contentful paint improved from 4.1s to 1.3s, and organic traffic increased by 38% in 3 months. That experience would help if your clone needs a polished UI, solid checkout flow, and a setup that’s easier for you to learn from than a typical theme-based approach.

Since you want to understand web apps better, I’d suggest working in milestones: first the structure and UI, then auth/data flow, then checkout/subscriptions, and finally refinement and walkthroughs so you can follow the code confidently. I’m comfortable keeping the pace flexible and working in a way that supports learning rather than just delivering code.

If the reference site has both card and PayPal checkout, which parts do you want to prioritize first for the learning build: the main user flow, the subscription system, or the payment integration?
